Hi Olivia,

Thanks for the heads-up and sorry again for the confusion. Looping in Rishi from Solutions Engineering who will send a direct Google Calendar invite (and include times converted to a couple of common zones).

Quick notes / workarounds we recommend when Calendly acts up:
1) Explicit timezone param: append ?timezone=Europe%2FLondon (or the appropriate IANA tz) to the Calendly URL; that forces the picker to show the requested zone.
2) Manual pick & confirm: share UTC times in the body (as I did below) and ask the recipient to confirm — guarantees everyone is aligned.
3) Cookie/Account issue: if a user has a Calendly account or cookies, it can override detection. Private/incognito mode usually shows correct browser locale.
4) Chili Piper: integrates differently and often avoids the tz cookie issue; if your team prefers it we can surface a Chili Piper link.

Important DST note: US DST begins on Mar 8, 2026, while UK DST begins on Mar 29, 2026. That can create confusing one-week offsets for cross-Atlantic scheduling. When possible we give UTC as the canonical time in the invite.

Rishi, could you please send the invite for one of Marissa's proposed slots (Mar 9 or Mar 10) and include the Google Meet link + ICS? Olivia, we’ll set it for your preferred timezone in the invite too.

Thanks all,

Marissa Cole
